precepts.text: There be nine things which I have judged in mine heart to be happy, and the tenth I will utter with my tongue: A man that hath joy of his children; and he that liveth to see the fall of his enemy. A man that hath joy of his children. Our brothers and sisters that have lost their husbands, that have lost their sons, they do not get to have the joy of their children. Their children are hanging on trees. Their daughters are hung on trees. Lives extinguished. They are not getting to enjoy their children. You are supposed to have joy of your children, but because an enemy has taken your children from you, hung your children on trees, murdered your children, you do not get that joy. And he that liveth to see the fall of his enemy. To see the fall of your enemies is therapy. God's therapy.
precepts.point: Verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth. Surely a man could say, surely there is a reward for your trauma, for the evils that have happened to us. God is going to give that to us. That is therapy. We talk about people with trauma and all that. God has given us therapy right there.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance.” Christianity will make you think you are not supposed to read this, but the Bible has it in there for you to rejoice. When you get to see your enemies get it, the people who have been oppressing us and doing all kinds of terrorist acts, and you get to see them get that justice, that's rejuvenation. It revitalizes your bones. “he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked”: that means smashing skulls and vertebrae and rib cages with your feet. That's a good thing. That's therapy.

The Bible names the great things we should look for, and one is joy of children: “There be nine things which I have judged in mine heart to be happy, and the tenth I will utter with my tongue: A man that hath joy of his children.” Our brothers and sisters who have lost their husbands and their sons don't get the joy of their children. Their children are hanging on trees; their daughters are hung on trees; lives extinguished. You are supposed to have joy of your children, but because an enemy has taken them from you, hung them on trees, murdered them, you don't get that joy.

“and he that liveth to see the fall of his enemy.” To see the fall of your enemies is therapy, God's therapy. People don't like it; give a damn. We talk about people with trauma; God has given us therapy right there.

That's why verse 11 begins with so: it gives the reason the vengeance of verse 10 is necessary. “So that a man shall say, Verily there is a reward for the righteous: verily he is a God that judgeth in the earth.” Surely there is a reward for our trauma, for the evils that have happened to us, and God is going to give it to us. When he beautifies the meek with salvation, it is us putting our enemies in chains and taking vengeance on them. Christianity isn't going to teach you that; these lying pastors and this Christianity garbage will completely destroy our people if we don't pull our heads out of it. And understand, if you teach that you want justice and vengeance, the enemy will call you hateful, and affliction comes with it. Program your mind for that. Don't think you can teach that the white man is the wicked of the earth and he'll leave you alone.

precepts.text: In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together. Why is that last one beautiful? Because it is hard for two different personalities to come together and be on one accord. Marriage takes time, brothers and sisters; it takes years and experience. But three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth. A poor man that is proud has no humility whatsoever: nobody can tell him anything, he has all the answers and no fruits in his life. That is how much the Lord hates pride.
precepts.point: Pride. Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. You think you know it all, you think you have all the wisdom and understanding; but pride is the progenitor of your destruction, because pride removes correction. You do not want to hear it. Pride isolates you, and pride precedes the collapse.
precepts.why:
This is how much the Lord hates pride. Sirach first shows what God loves: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren the Lord loves; the love of neighbors the Lord loves. And a man and wife that agree together: why is that beautiful? Because it's hard for two different personalities to come together and be on the same accord. That's why marriage takes time, brothers and sisters. It isn't overnight; it takes years and experience.

Now the negative: “Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.” He is offended at their life. A negro that's poor and proud: I hate that negro, I hate his soul, I hate everything about him. How can you be that way?

It means you have no humility whatsoever. Nobody can tell you anything; you have all the answers, but no fruits in your life, no solutions, no shame. That is the pride that goes before destruction, and God's soul hates it.

precepts.text: In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, and a man and a wife that agree together. All three are unity in righteousness. It is not that oogly googly feeling about your neighbor; it is unity in righteousness. A sanctified holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before the Lord. Anything other than that is not beautiful; the Lord is not beautified. Remember how Paul wrote to the different schools: you are puffed up, there are all types of schisms among you. That is not unity. To be unified means to come together in holiness and righteousness the way God meant it to be.
precepts.point: If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not talking about gang banging, not the fraternities, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly foolishness some of us came out of. This unification is talking about being unified in Christ. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. To be united in the Lord is true unity.
precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Some think this is just talking about a bunch of Negroes coming together, a bunch of brothers together, and that's beautiful. No, it is much more than that. If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not gang banging, not the Hoovers, not the Omegas, Kappas and Alphas, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly nonsense some of us came out of. It is being unified in Christ; hence the name Israel United in Christ.

Sirach shows what unity God is beautified by: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren in what? In righteousness. The love of neighbours is not that oogly googly feeling, that's my neighbor, we're good friends; it is unity in righteousness, someone that shows care for their nation and their people. A man and a wife that agree together, in righteousness: a sanctified holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before the Lord.

Anything other than that is not beautiful, and the Lord is not beautified by it. Remember how Paul wrote to the different schools: you are puffed up, there are all types of schisms among you. That is not unity. To be unified means to come together in holiness and righteousness, the way God meant it to be and the way Christ told us to be. And that unification of the nation of Israel is the highest known threat to this evil world; it scares them.

precepts.text: Three things beautiful before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, and a man and wife that agree together, on the commandments, not on the curtains.
precepts.point: Gather yourselves together, O nation not desired: in the last days we gather with the believers who fear the Lord and make things common, because you cannot say to your brother be warmed and filled and go your way; true charity shows in adversity.
precepts.why:
“In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.” The Lord puts the unity of brethren first. Then the love of neighbours: the charity, the long-suffering.

Then “a man and a wife that agree together.” Agree on what? The commandments. That is not talking about arguing over the curtains. Brother, when did you become a fashion designer, an interior decorator? Let your wife handle that. The agreement God counts beautiful is agreement in keeping his law.

This is what the gathering of Zephaniah 2:1 has to look like. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: the nation hated upon the earth has to come together in the last days. But as we gather, we have to fix our character flaws, show ourselves friendly, and endeavor to keep the unity, and endeavor is an enduring word, not one to be taken lightly.

Unity of brethren does not mean you cannot correct one another or admonish one another. It means you expect highly of each other. We need correction, admonishment, counsel and advice amongst each other. Those who push you toward hard things, who tell you the harsh truth when a lie would be easier, are your people. That is how the gathered nation stands up beautiful before God and men.

precepts.text: If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, give her a bill of divorce, and let her go. This is the worldly marriage of a man trying to repent whose wife keeps the traps going. It is not the biblical marriage: once married in this truth she is yours for life unless she commits adultery, and there is no divorce in the Bible.
precepts.point: Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her, because she was his portion and was meant to destroy him. Some are not made to make it; if your spirit is not girded, one of these temptations takes you.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
“whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.” A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man. But what about the man who complains of a wicked woman and claims he is not wicked himself? If that is true, he will find a way to escape. Sirach shows the way: “If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.”

This is the brother in the world trying to repent, trying to get his house in order and straighten it out, while his wife keeps up the traps of Ecclesiastes 7:26: her heart snares and nets, her hands as bands, creating chaos and assignments so he can't get to camp, to the brothers, to the meetings. She doesn't want to listen. Then let her go. And it goes both ways; it is about you men too.

But understand: this is not talking about a biblical marriage. Once you get married in this truth, she is yours for life, unless she commits adultery. There is no divorce in the Bible, and we don't dissolve marriages up in here; it is written in our rules. This is for those coming in from outside this truth, with all kinds of situations.

So the man who pleases God escapes from her. But if you allow yourself to be destroyed, you were indeed wicked, and the woman sent to you was your portion for real.

precepts.text: In the last days men shall be lovers of their own selves, without natural affection (minors, the same sex), trucebreakers, despisers of those that are good (I just don't like that brother; what does he do? teach the word of God), traitors, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God. Love pleasure more than God and you make excuses to feed the lust and stop showing up for the work.
precepts.point: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. Many of you see America as a gorgeous woman and are mesmerized; every pleasure is available in her. Many brothers fall by harlots, and you do not have to pick up a prostitute to be dealing with the mother of all harlots.
precepts.why:
“Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.” Many of you look at America as a gorgeous, beautiful woman, and you are mesmerized. In America you can have every kind of pleasure. A lot of brothers fall by harlots, and just because you are not picking up a prostitute doesn’t mean you aren’t out there dealing with harlots. This is the mother of all harlots. And remember, sin is pleasurable.

Paul describes the last days: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection”: some like young minors, some like people of the same sex. “Trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good.” I don’t like that brother. Why not? Every time I look up he is doing something. What, teaching the word of God? We have spirits like that sitting among us, worried about petty things while this truth is trying to get us out of here.

“Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.” That is a big issue. If you love pleasure more than you love God, you start making excuses to feed that lust, and you find yourself not around doing the Lord’s work as much. Everybody asks, what’s wrong with that brother’s spirit? He loves his lust more than God.

That is what it means to stumble at the beauty of the woman and desire her for pleasure: to love America’s pleasures more than God. The brothers and sisters who fade away, this is your gut check.

precepts.text: Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing affliction with the people of God over the pleasures of sin for a season. He gave up status in Egypt, so the nice job is no excuse. This is temporary; be robotic and get the feelings out of it, because feelings get you killed.
precepts.point: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. Many of you see America as a gorgeous woman and are mesmerized; every pleasure is available in her. Many brothers fall by harlots, and you do not have to pick up a prostitute to be dealing with the mother of all harlots.
precepts.why:
Don’t stumble at the beauty of the woman, America, or desire her for pleasure. Moses shows the way: “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.” He wanted nothing to do with Egypt or the king of Egypt, because he knew he was an Israelite and God had chosen him for a mighty work, to deliver his people out of captivity.

Some of y’all say, it’s not that bad, and you show it by your mentality and your actions. Moses lived it up and had status in Egypt, like some of you have nice jobs and status in America. So you can’t say it’s because of that. Moses gave it all up; why can’t you?

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” For a season means it is temporary. It is only here for so long, and then destruction and salvation. That is the mindset we have to have.

We have to be robotic and get the feelings out of it. Nobody cares how you feel; feelings get you killed. Choose affliction with the people of God over the passing pleasures of Babylon.

precepts.text: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees' excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. Seeing seven crowns and ten toes on the Statue of Liberty should make you say the Bible is true, not God bless America. Stop gazing at her pleasures; wake up.
precepts.point: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. Many of you see America as a gorgeous woman and are mesmerized; every pleasure is available in her. Many brothers fall by harlots, and you do not have to pick up a prostitute to be dealing with the mother of all harlots.
precepts.why:
The class is The Beauty and the Beast, and this is the beauty. When sin takes over, you can’t see clearly. Isaiah says: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency.” That is how they perceive her, and how many of our people see America.

But you shouldn’t look at America like that. When you see the Statue of Liberty, you shouldn’t say, God bless America. Some of y’all feel real proud seeing things like that. When I first looked at it, I saw seven crowns on her head and ten toes, and I said, wow, the Bible is a true book. Not, Lady Liberty, I love you. The Bible is spot on.

“Shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” This place is going to be destroyed. You shouldn’t be sitting there gazing at her and mesmerized by her pleasures. You know this place is coming to an end. Wake up. Don’t stumble at her beauty.

precepts.text: The well-favoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms and families through her witchcrafts. They sold us, which is how we got here. If you are down with America you are down with the devil.
precepts.point: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. Many of you see America as a gorgeous woman and are mesmerized; every pleasure is available in her. Many brothers fall by harlots, and you do not have to pick up a prostitute to be dealing with the mother of all harlots.
precepts.why:
Sirach warns not to stumble at the beauty of a woman, and the Lord calls this nation a harlot. Nahum says: “Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts.” The well-favoured harlot: some of you are caught up with her. I hope it isn’t a lot of you.

“That selleth nations through her whoredoms.” She sells nations. They sold us; that is how we got over here. “And families through her witchcrafts.”

Meaning what? If you are down with America, you are down with the devil. That is what the Bible is telling us. Nahum saw the same thing John the Revelator saw: the judgment of the great harlot that sits upon many waters, and upon her forehead “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” An abomination is something the Lord hates and despises.

So her beauty is the beauty of a harlot and a witch that sold us. Desire her not for pleasure.

precepts.text: Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins and receive not of her plagues. Mystery Babylon, mother of harlots and abominations. The Lord is still sending plagues, remember the pandemic; come out spiritually so that is not your condemnation.
precepts.point: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. Many of you see America as a gorgeous woman and are mesmerized; every pleasure is available in her. Many brothers fall by harlots, and you do not have to pick up a prostitute to be dealing with the mother of all harlots.
precepts.why:
She says in her heart, “I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.” Some of y’all have taken on the characteristics of America, and it is time to shake that off. She is “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH”, and an abomination is what the Lord hates and despises. So it is time to come up out of her.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.”

That ye receive not of her plagues, because the Lord is still sending plagues. Y’all remember the pandemic. Stay with the Lord and come up out of her spiritually, so that her condemnation is not your condemnation.

That is what it means not to stumble at the beauty of the woman: don’t be mesmerized by her or desire her for pleasure, but come out of her, because her judgment is coming.

precepts.text: I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations, terrorists, and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom and defile thy brightness. Wisdom is double, Job 11:6: contextually the king of Tyrus, prophetically America, which everyone thought untouchable. It decays from the inside out, then the finale with the ten horns, and its pretence of moral world police is defiled.
precepts.point: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure. Many of you see America as a gorgeous woman and are mesmerized; every pleasure is available in her. Many brothers fall by harlots, and you do not have to pick up a prostitute to be dealing with the mother of all harlots.
precepts.why:
“Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations.” Contextually this is spoken to the king of Tyrus, who was said to be wiser than Daniel. But when you read the scriptures, a passage may speak contextually of one nation and prophetically of another, because the Lord shows “the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” Prophetically, this is Babylon the Great, America.

Who are the strangers, the terrible of the nations? The Allahu Akbar type strangers. Another word for it would be terrorists. “And they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom.” A lot of people thought America could never be touched. The Lord is showing you otherwise. When she begins to fall, she will be destroyed from the inside out, decaying, and then comes the great finale with the ten horns.

“And they shall defile thy brightness.” America likes to put on as if she is righteous, playing the moral world police, while she goes into countries, steals presidents and bombs everybody. That brightness will be defiled.

So don’t stumble at her beauty. The beauty of her wisdom and her brightness are exactly what the Lord has marked for the sword.

precepts.text: In three things I was beautified before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together. The agreement is not the same music or food; she agrees to follow the scriptures for a wife without contingencies, and he agrees to do the same as a husband. That is what is beautiful in God's eyes.
precepts.point: He took her uprightly and they aged together mercifully, and with age comes beauty, love, and passion, not whimsical movie feelings. Stop chasing a feeling; get your mind like Tobit's. If even a majority of families moved in that spirit, how much stronger are we as a people for the time of trouble to come. Weddings are not done here for anyone who has not proved for three years.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Tobias prayed, and Sara “said with him, Amen.” She agreed, because her mind was on her lord; she didn't say, wait, what about the house, what about the gifts. Sirach gives more insight into the character that strengthens marriage: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

A man and a wife that agree together. The agreement is not that you both like the same music, the same colors, the same food; that's part of the aging stuff. The agreement is this: she agrees to follow the scriptures that pertain to her as a wife, whether or not there are contingencies, because the Bible gives no contingencies for a wife's behavior. You do or you don't. And he agrees to do the same as a husband.

You agree in God that you are going to follow his order of marriage, running it with your responsibilities as a wife and yours as a husband the way the Bible says. That is what is beautiful in God's eyes, because it will work the way he intended when you do those things.

precepts.text: We used to bring this out only for the dead beat who would not work. But a man who leaves everything else unfilled makes her maintain that role too, and she was never constructed for it.
precepts.point: The title of husband no more came with the understanding of it than the title of soldier, officer, captain or deacon did. You have to go through the paces.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

precepts.text: Of the things judged in the heart to be happy: a man that hath joy of his children, and he that liveth to see the fall of his enemy. That is something to rejoice over.
precepts.point: Rome, you just slaughtered a thousand Israelites, let me pray for you, is the stupidest thought there is, and it is the idea the black Christian holds and preaches.

precepts.text: Of the woman came the beginning of sin; the warning runs from Eve through the mothers.
precepts.point: From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household; of the woman came the beginning of sin. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.”

From Eve to Rachel the scriptures warn how sin enters through the household. Eve was beguiled by the serpent; Rachel stole her father's images and hid them, and so strange gods came into the house of Jacob, which had to be put away before he could go up to Bethel. Sisters, stay in the spirit and guard against the serpent's beguiling as the mothers were beguiled.

precepts.text: Better to live with a lion or a dragon than to keep house with a wicked woman.
precepts.point: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than with a brawling woman in a wide house. No mansion is big enough to share with a woman who chest-bumps, gets in her man's face, and is shalom at the school but calls a man out of his name at home.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

precepts.why:
“It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.” No mansion is big enough to share with a woman who chest-bumps, gets in her man's face, and is shalom at the school but calls a man out of his name at home.

Ecclesiasticus says it stronger: “I had rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, than to keep house with a wicked woman.” Better to live with a lion or a dragon than to keep house with a wicked woman. The corner of the housetop and the lion's den are the same choice: anywhere but a wide house with a brawling woman.
